name: Bright Hands, Dark Harvest: The Geneware Labor Question
description: A Vantablack-adjacent independent documentary that began as a licensed exploration of geneware labor economics and evolved, during production, into a damning account of how genetically modified agricultural workers in the Vertical Farm belt are legally classified as 'biological infrastructure' rather than persons, exempting their employers from labor protections. The film features hidden-feed testimony from eleven modified workers and leaked Sable Charter classification documents. Vantablack Media withdrew its distribution agreement three days before release, but the director had already seeded the complete neural-feed version to seventeen pirate mesh nodes.
cultural_impact: Directly inspired the Seam Rights advocacy movement's 2213 legal challenge to the 'biological infrastructure' classification, which failed but generated unprecedented public coverage.
story_hooks: One of the eleven anonymous worker-witnesses has been identified by their employer using BCI signature analysis from the neural-feed testimony and is now missing.
The leaked Sable Charter documents in the film contain a classification code that, if decoded, reveals a much larger category of persons currently designated as non-persons.
A Tier 4 food executive who appears briefly in background footage of a Vertical Farm inspection tour is now running for a Sable Charter seat and will do anything to keep the film suppressed.
